layout.title: How a Septic Tank Works

shows.does: the pit is dug and the toilet pipe grows into it
brown sewage rises to the rim and spills onto the lawn
a concrete tank appears, fills, and sludge sinks to its floor
a dark grease layer floats up to the top
a T outlet pipe grows and clear water runs out of it
puddles spread over the lawn at the pipe's end
a gravel bed and a holed pipe appear, water spreads and soaks down
a septic tank: solids settle, scum floats, clear water flows on
a brown sludge layer rises in the tank
a riser grows to the surface and the sludge is pumped out
rain runs down the open riser into the tank
a heavy lid closes the riser
grass covers the tank and the duck bobs safely inside
calm lawn over the tank with its lid and the drain field

layout.why: The old septic layout: the pit and tank in the cut, the outlet and drain field to the right in the face; a flushed rubber duck rides in from the toilet pipe and stays in the tank. The camera follows the sewage from the pipe through the tank to the field, then the riser and lid.

sentences.text: If you dig a pit for your toilet, you have a septic tank.
But sewage fills it and spills onto the lawn.
So a concrete tank lets the solids sink.
But grease floats to the top of the tank.
So a T-shaped pipe below the grease lets clear water out.
But that pipe floods one spot of the lawn.
So holed pipes in gravel spread it into soil.
But now as water soaks away, sludge piles up.
So you add a riser to pump the sludge.
But rain pours down the open riser.
So you bolt a heavy lid on top.
Flush the toilet, and it all flows away.
Congratulations, you have built a septic tank.
